sentence_stem: Had the committee been consulted earlier,
correct_completion: the policy would almost certainly have taken a different shape.
full_sentence: Had the committee been consulted earlier, the policy would almost certainly have taken a different shape.
acceptable_variants: the policy would probably have looked quite different.
the outcome might have been very different.

options.text: the policy would be drafted differently today.
options.why_wrong: 'Today' conflicts with the past time frame set by the inverted 'Had' clause, which refers to an earlier moment.

options.text: so the policy was adopted without changes.
options.why_wrong: This uses a simple past statement of what actually happened and introduces a cause, but the stem requires a hypothetical result.

options.text: the policy would almost certainly have taken a different shape.
the committee has already been consulted.
options.why_wrong: The present perfect states a fact and contradicts the counterfactual meaning that the inverted 'Had' clause sets up.

grammar_focus: Inverted third conditional (Had + subject + past participle)
explanation: The inverted form 'Had + subject + past participle' replaces 'if', so the main clause needs 'would have' followed by a past participle. Options with present, simple past or present perfect forms break this counterfactual pattern.
translation: Si el comité hubiera sido consultado antes, la política habría tomado casi seguramente una forma diferente.
